solution.full_text:
1. The correct answer is option $(1)$ which is E, A, D, C, B.
2. The catalytic cycle of an enzyme action can be described in the following steps.
3. $(1)$ First, the substrate binds to the active site of the enzyme, fitting into the active site.
4. $(2)$ The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape, fitting more tightly around the substrate.
5. $(3)$ The active site of the enzyme, now in close proximity of the substrate breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate and the new enzyme-product complex is formed.
6. $(4)$ The enzyme releases the products of the reaction and the free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule of the substrate and run through the catalytic cycle once again.
7. Options $(2)$, $(3)$ and $(4)$ are incorrect as the steps mentioned are in the wrong sequence.

question.full_text:
As per ABO blood grouping system, the blood group of father is $\mathrm{B^{+}}$, mother is $\mathrm{A^{+}}$ and child is $\mathrm{O^{+}}$. Their respective genotype can be
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
(A) $\mathrm{I^{B}i/I^{A}i/ii}$
(B) $\mathrm{I^{B}I^{B}/I^{A}I^{A}/ii}$
(C) $\mathrm{I^{A}I^{B}/iI^{A}/I^{B}i}$
(D) $\mathrm{I^{A}i/I^{B}i/I^{A}i}$
(E) $\mathrm{iI^{B}/iI^{A}/I^{A}I^{B}}$
(1) A only
(2) B only
(3) C & B only
(4) D & E only
question.html:
As per ABO blood grouping system, the blood group of father is B+, mother is A+ and child is O+. Their respective genotype can be
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
  1. (A) IBi/IAi/ii
  2. (B) IBIB/IAIA/ii
  3. (C) IAIB/iIA/IBi
  4. (D) IAi/IBi/IAi
  5. (E) iIB/iIA/IAIB
  1. (1)A only
  2. (2)B only
  3. (3)C & B only
  4. (4)D & E only
question.stem:
As per ABO blood grouping system, the blood group of father is $\mathrm{B^{+}}$, mother is $\mathrm{A^{+}}$ and child is $\mathrm{O^{+}}$. Their respective genotype can be
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

statements.label: A
statements.text: $\mathrm{I^{B}i/I^{A}i/ii}$

statements.label: B
statements.text: $\mathrm{I^{B}I^{B}/I^{A}I^{A}/ii}$

statements.label: C
statements.text: $\mathrm{I^{A}I^{B}/iI^{A}/I^{B}i}$

statements.label: D
statements.text: $\mathrm{I^{A}i/I^{B}i/I^{A}i}$

statements.label: E
statements.text: $\mathrm{iI^{B}/iI^{A}/I^{A}I^{B}}$

solution.full_text:
1. Genotype of father with blood group $\mathrm{B^{+}} = \mathrm{I^{B}i/iI^{B}}$
2. Genotype of mother with blood group $\mathrm{A^{+}} = \mathrm{I^{A}i/iI^{A}}$
3. Genotype of child with blood group $\mathrm{O^{+}} = \mathrm{ii}$
4. Hence only ‘A’ is correct.
solution.html:
1. Genotype of father with blood group B+ = IBi/iIB
  2. Genotype of mother with blood group A+ = IAi/iIA
  3. Genotype of child with blood group O+ = ii
  4. Hence only ‘A’ is correct.
steps: Genotype of father with blood group $\mathrm{B^{+}} = \mathrm{I^{B}i/iI^{B}}$
Genotype of mother with blood group $\mathrm{A^{+}} = \mathrm{I^{A}i/iI^{A}}$
Genotype of child with blood group $\mathrm{O^{+}} = \mathrm{ii}$
Hence only ‘A’ is correct.
printed_lines: Genotype of father with blood group B^{+} = I^{B}i/iI^{B}
Genotype of mother with blood group A^{+} = I^{A}i/iI^{A}
Genotype of child with blood group O^{+} = ii

steps: Blood group O is only possible with genotype $ii$, so the child is $ii$ and got one $i$ allele from each parent.
So the father (group B) must be $I^{B}i$ and the mother (group A) must be $I^{A}i$.
Statement A ($I^{B}i/I^{A}i/ii$) matches. B fails because homozygous parents cannot have an $ii$ child, and C, D and E give the wrong phenotypes.
Only A is correct, which is option $1$.
ai_solution.html:
1. Blood group O is only possible with genotype ii, so the child is ii and got one i allele from each parent.
  2. So the father (group B) must be IBi and the mother (group A) must be IAi.
  3. Statement A (IBi/IAi/ii) matches. B fails because homozygous parents cannot have an ii child, and C, D and E give the wrong phenotypes.
  4. Only A is correct, which is option 1.
ai_solution.why: An O child (ii) needs an i allele from each parent, so the B father must be I^Bi and the A mother I^Ai; only A fits.

chapter.name: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
chapter.why: The answer turns on ABO multiple alleles (IA, IB, i) and their inheritance, so only heterozygous IBi x IAi parents can produce an ii (O) child.

subtopics.name: Pleiotropy, Multiple Alleles & Polygenic Inheritance
subtopics.why: The answer depends on the ABO blood group being controlled by the multiple alleles IA, IB and i, so B+ and A+ parents with an O child must be IBi and IAi with the child ii.

step_list: Child is O, so the child's genotype must be ii
Each parent must therefore carry an i allele: father B is IBi, mother A is IAi
Check the five statements in father/mother/child order against IBi / IAi / ii and pick the option that lists only the matching one
difficulty.why: Medium: the genetics is one recalled idea (an O child forces both parents to carry i), but five slash-separated genotype triples have to be read in father/mother/child order, and statement E has the right parents with the wrong child, so option 4 survives a careless check. Option 2 (homozygous parents) and option 3 (father written as AB) fall at once.
difficulty.what_makes_it_hard: Statement E is the altered line: the parents' genotypes are correct but written with the alleles reversed (iIB, iIA), and only the child's genotype (IAIB instead of ii) makes it wrong. Statement D also looks plausible until you notice that father and mother are swapped.

source.note: Option (3) printed as 'C & B only' (order as in source).
